name: South Carolina
overview: In South Carolina each county's official in charge of collecting delinquent taxes (usually the Delinquent Tax Collector or Treasurer) sells tax-delinquent real estate at a public auction at the courthouse or another convenient place in the county, after advertising it under the heading "Delinquent Tax Sale"; most counties hold one sale a year in the fall. The winning bid must be paid in full on the day of the sale by cash, cashier's check, certified check or money order. The owner, or a mortgage or judgment creditor, may redeem the property within twelve months from the date of the sale by paying the taxes, costs and interest on the bid amount of 3% in the first three months, 6% in months four to six, 9% in months seven to nine and 12% in the last three months, capped at the amount of the bid. If the property is not redeemed, the official makes a tax title to the purchaser.

counties.how_to_bid: Pre-register in person with the Tax Collector's Office between October 1 and November 6, 2026 (9 AM to 5 PM) and pay a non-refundable $10 registration fee; there is no registration on sale day. You must be present to bid. Properties are auctioned in the order advertised to the highest bidder; with no bid, the Forfeited Land Commission takes the property. All bids must be paid in full by 5:00 PM the same day by cash, cashier's check or money order. All sales are final and failure to comply draws a $500.00 fine. The owner has one year to redeem; interest runs 3%, 6%, 9% or 12% by quarter and may not exceed the bid. Deposit not stated.

counties.how_to_bid: Register online only (the office no longer takes registrations) and pay the non-refundable $25.00 fee when completing the form; no registration on sale day. Bidding is open, using your numbered bidder card; the auctioneer opens each parcel with a bid for the Forfeited Land Commission, and parcels go in the order of the newspaper ads. Pay by money order or certified funds only (no personal checks) by 5:00 p.m. on sale day. All sales are final. The owner may redeem within twelve months; interest runs 3%, 6%, 9% or 12% by quarter, not exceeding the opening bid. Deposit not stated.

counties.how_to_bid: Register in person at 111 Law Range St. (8:30 AM to 4:30 PM) or by email between October 12 and November 30 with a Social Security card, valid driver's license and mailing information; companies add a W-9 and an authorization statement. No one registers after November 30 or on sale day, and you must be present to bid. It is a live auction; bidding runs until a high bid is reached. Pay the full bid in cash or exact-amount certified funds by 4:30 PM on sale day, or a $500 penalty per bid applies. Property is subject to a 12-month redemption period with interest of 3%, 6%, 9% or 12% by quarter, capped at the starting bid. Deposit not stated.

counties.how_to_bid: Get the bidder registration and bidder information forms from the Delinquent Tax Office (linked under Forms on the county page). Under the county's 2025 rules (the newest posted), the form was due by 5:00 PM on the Friday before the sale, bids had to be paid in cash, cashier's check, certified check or money order (no personal checks) by 5 PM on the day of the sale, and a $500 penalty applied per unpaid or cancelled bid; people who owe delinquent taxes themselves could not bid. The opening bid is the Forfeited Land Commission bid. Each sale carries a 12-month redemption period with 3%, 6%, 9% or 12% interest by quarter, capped at the opening bid. 2026 rules, deposit and time not stated.
